plan.title: Hosted-bot access without Tailscale: TLS passthrough relay at <name>.mcp.overdeck.ai (relay add-on)
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

references.label: S-C machine tunnel and TLS listener
S-E settings, enable flow, e2e, user docs
PAN-5486 Grok Bot docs and core pins (overlapping docs)

metadata.sizeJustification: Code touches only two subsystems (src/dashboard, src/lib) plus their tests. The count passes 6 because the two-segment subsystem rule counts each single documentation file (configuration/bots.mdx, configuration/mcp.mdx, changelog.d/pan-5058.md) and the checkpoint record folders (integrations/grok-bot, .pan/drafts) as separate subsystems. The relay build itself is already split out into seven sibling issues #5490-#5496 (PRD D-1).

narratives.Problem: Hosted bots (Grok Bot, the xAI API, Meta's Muse) cannot run the Overdeck connector and need a public HTTPS /mcp. Today the only route is Tailscale Funnel, which most users will not set up. Grok Bot cannot use the connector at all (no WebRTC egress, PAN-5242), and Public MCP has never been run live with Grok Bot or Muse. The operator ordered a live Grok Bot run over Funnel before any relay code, because the relay reuses that exact OAuth path.
narratives.Proposal: PRD .pan/drafts/PAN-5058.md designs the whole feature: an Overdeck-run TLS passthrough relay at <label>.mcp.overdeck.ai that forwards ciphertext by SNI to an outbound tunnel from the user's machine, where TLS ends with a certificate the machine gets itself through TLS-ALPN-01. The build is split into seven sibling issues (#5490-#5496). This issue does what must come first: log refused OAuth client registrations (W-1), run Grok Bot live over Funnel (CP-1, W-2), accept private-use redirect URI schemes only if CP-1 shows Grok Bot needs them (W-3), run Meta Muse live (CP-2, W-4), make the Grok Bot docs say what CP-1 found (W-5), and amend the PAN-4927 PRD so it describes the relay as a second public route that forwards ciphertext only (W-6).
narratives.NonGoals:
- Building the relay service, tunnel client, TLS listener, certificates, Settings panel, GTS fallback or CT watch in this issue; those are siblings #5490-#5496
- Metering relay MCP bytes against the 50 GB relay allowance
- ARI certificate renewals
- /hooks/* triggers over the relay
- Any plaintext MCP relay or TLS termination of user hostnames on overdeck.ai
- Agents deploying the relay, changing DNS, running wrangler deploy or filing the Let's Encrypt rate-limit override
- Running or automating Tailscale for the user beyond the one-time CP-1 setup on the operator's machine
- Changing /mcp tools, token scopes or OAuth access levels
- Marking any live checkpoint row passed without a dated live run

autoDecisions.summary: Split the feature into this issue plus seven sibling issues #5490-#5496 (S-A to S-G); siblings are blocked by this issue.
autoDecisions.rationale: The full design spans account service, a new relay service, contracts, gate/auth, TLS/ACME, UI and many docs, far past the 25-file / 6-subsystem plan limit. The operator ordered the Grok Bot checkpoint before any relay code, and this issue carries the PRD to main, so it naturally comes first.

autoDecisions.summary: Relay hostnames are random 12-character labels allocated per machine by the account service, sticky across toggles, at most 5 active per account.
autoDecisions.rationale: Every certificate is public in CT logs, so a login or machine name in the hostname would publish it. Per machine because TLS ends on each machine. The cap bounds Let's Encrypt use.

autoDecisions.summary: The machine authenticates to the relay with 10-minute HMAC relay tickets from the account service, never with its device token.
autoDecisions.rationale: A device token can revoke devices and delete the account; the relay must not hold it. Tickets let a Fly app verify offline and make revocation and add-on lapse take effect within about 10 minutes.

autoDecisions.summary: Wire protocol: one control WebSocket plus one data WebSocket per inbound stream, at mcp-relay.overdeck.ai (outside the user wildcard).
autoDecisions.rationale: WebSocket already frames bytes, so no custom multiplexer, flow control or head-of-line handling; one extra round trip per TCP connection is cheap for MCP.

autoDecisions.summary: Relay requests are marked by tagging the decrypted TLSSocket and handing it to the HTTP listeners, never by a loopback proxy plus header.
autoDecisions.rationale: An untagged loopback request is the trusted local operator, so a header-based proxy fails open on any bug; a tagged socket fails closed. The ChannelSocket path in channel-listener.ts is the precedent.

autoDecisions.summary: Pre-write the custom-scheme redirect URI fix (W-3) but run it only if CP-1 shows the refusal; otherwise cancel it.
autoDecisions.rationale: Forum reports show Grok Bot's OAuth registers a cursor:// callback, and Overdeck rejects the whole registration for any non-https URI, but what Grok Bot sends to Overdeck is unverified. The issue comment says to fix Public MCP and OAuth inside this issue if the live run fails.

autoDecisions.summary: Meta Muse stays in scope as live checkpoint CP-2.
autoDecisions.rationale: Third-party Muse guides say Muse connects to any public streamable-HTTP MCP URL with credentials from a secure prompt, so it is not directory-only.

autoDecisions.summary: No ARI renewals; renew 30 days before expiry with the same identifier, back off 1 h doubling to 24 h after failures.
autoDecisions.rationale: Let's Encrypt exempts same-identifier renewals from the per-domain limit, acme-client 5.4.0 has no ARI support, and the 5-failures-per-hour and 5-per-identifier limits have no override.

autoDecisions.summary: Relay MCP bytes are not metered against the 50 GB relay allowance in this release.
autoDecisions.rationale: MCP traffic is small JSON, and metering would require the Fly relay to report into the connect Durable Objects; the relay logs bytes so real use can be measured.

items.title: Write one activity entry for every refused MCP client registration

expected_outputs: mcp-oauth.test.ts passes including the new refused-registration audit tests

narrative.Action: PRD W-1. In routes/mcp-oauth.ts add optional McpOAuthRouteDeps.audit (default emitActivityEntry) and redirectOriginsOf(body). Replace the register handler's local `invalid` helper with one `refuse(status, errorBody, body?)` that writes exactly one activity entry { source: 'dashboard', level: 'warn', message: 'MCP client registration refused', details: JSON.stringify({ error, redirectOrigins }) } and returns the response. Use it for all four refusals: wrong media type, body over 16 KiB, invalid JSON (redirectOrigins [] because the body was never parsed) and a non-ok registerClient result (origins from the parsed body: `${protocol}//${host}` of the first 5 redirect URIs, '<invalid>' for unparseable). Never log a path, query, fragment, token or code.

items.title: Given a registration whose redirect_uris is ["cursor://anysphere.cursor-mcp/oauth/callback?x=1"], when POST /oauth/mcp/register answers 400, then the audit spy receives exactly one entry whose details JSON has redirectOrigins ["cursor://anysphere.cursor-mcp"] and contains neither "/oauth/callback" nor "x=1"
Given a text/plain body, a 17 KiB JSON body, or invalid JSON, when POST /oauth/mcp/register answers 400, then the audit spy receives exactly one entry with redirectOrigins []
Given a valid https registration, when POST /oauth/mcp/register answers 201, then the audit spy receives no entry
Record the authorization scheme (never the value) in the public /mcp audit entry

expected_outputs: public-mcp-funnel.test.ts passes including the authScheme cases

narrative.Action: PRD W-1b. In public-mcp-funnel.ts add exported authSchemeOf(headers): no or empty authorization header -> 'none'; trimmed value split on whitespace: 2+ parts with first part 'bearer' (case-insensitive) -> 'bearer'; exactly one part -> 'bare'; otherwise 'other'. Change the audit details from JSON.stringify({ clientId }) to JSON.stringify({ clientId, authScheme }) where authScheme is authSchemeOf(headers) for surface 'POST /mcp' and undefined otherwise. Never log the header value. CP-1 reads the token form from this field because a 401 alone cannot distinguish a bare token from a missing or expired one.

items.title: Given a Funnel POST /mcp with Authorization 'odk_<64 hex>', when the middleware audits it, then details has authScheme 'bare'; with 'Bearer odk_<64 hex>' it has 'bearer'; with no header 'none'; with 'Basic x' 'other'
Given any audited public request in the test, when its details string is read, then it contains no 'odk_' substring
CP-1: run Grok Bot live against Public MCP over Tailscale Funnel and record the result

expected_outputs: verification.md prints a dated 'Live run ... (PAN-5058 CP-1)' heading
the PRD 'Checkpoint results' section has a dated CP-1 line

narrative.Action: PRD W-2 and D-16. Step 0: the operator's dashboard serves main without W-1/W-1b, so run `npm run build` here and start a peer dashboard that shares ~/.overdeck: `ln -sf "$PWD/dist/dashboard/server.js" ~/.overdeck/tmp/pan5058-cp1-server.js` (path must not contain dist/dashboard/server.js or the orphan reaper kills it), then in the background `OVERDECK_DISABLE_DEACON=1 PORT=3041 API_PORT=3041 OVERDECK_TRUSTED_ORIGINS=https://<machine>.<tailnet>.ts.net node ~/.overdeck/tmp/pan5058-cp1-server.js`. Check /api/health on 3041 and that a text/plain POST /oauth/mcp/register on 3041 produces the 'MCP client registration refused' activity entry. Operator steps are only credential steps: install Tailscale with sudo and sign in, sign in to Grok Bot. Ask with `pan tell flywheel-orchestrator` plus a needs-you note; `pan task block` this item while waiting. The agent does the rest: admin-console HTTPS certificates and funnel node attribute (browser, operator signed in), Public MCP on, the three tailscale funnel paths pointed at http://127.0.0.1:3041, curl the discovery document from outside the tailnet, add the custom MCP connector in Grok Bot with https://<host>:8443/mcp, approve the sign-in in the peer UI at http://127.0.0.1:3041, ask Grok Bot to list conversations. Record a dated section in integrations/grok-bot/docs/verification.md with one row per FR-1 fact: registration (201 or the W-1 entry's redirectOrigins), PKCE method in the authorize URL, approval and token exchange, token form from the W-1b authScheme field (never inferred from a status code; no /mcp call observed => 'Not run'), list_conversations, 'redirect_uri not allowed' seen or not. Copy it to the PRD 'Checkpoint results'. Decision rule: custom-scheme refusal => W-3 then re-run; another Overdeck-side failure => fix here with a regression test, documented as W-2a in the PRD; xAI-side failure => record and file a follow-up issue. Never record a token or code; never mark a row passed without the dated run. Stop the peer and remove the Funnel paths after W-4.

items.title: Given the live run happened, when verification.md is read, then it shows a section headed 'Live run 2026-<mm>-<dd> (PAN-5058 CP-1)' with one row each for registration, PKCE, token exchange, token form, list_conversations and redirect_uri error, each reading Passed, Failed: <cause> or Not run: <reason>

Given the registration row, when it is read, then it names the redirect origins taken from the W-1 activity entry or the 201 response, and verification.md contains no odk_, odr_ or authorization code value
Given the PRD .pan/drafts/PAN-5058.md, when 'Checkpoint results' is read, then it contains a dated CP-1 line that matches the verification.md outcome
Given the token form row, when it is read, then its value is the authScheme from a 'Public MCP POST /mcp' activity entry (bearer, bare, other or none) or 'Not run: no /mcp call observed'
Accept private-use redirect URI schemes in MCP client registration (only if CP-1 shows the refusal)

expected_outputs: oauth-flow and oauth-service tests pass including the new private-scheme cases

narrative.Action: PRD W-3 and D-15. Run only when W-2 recorded a refused registration whose redirectOrigins include a non-http(s) scheme; otherwise `pan task cancel` this item with the reason 'CP-1 showed no custom-scheme refusal'. In oauth-flow.ts add PRIVATE_SCHEME /^[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*:$/, BLOCKED_SCHEMES {javascript:, data:, file:, blob:, vbscript:, about:, ws:, wss:, ftp:} and isPrivateUseScheme(url); redirectUriProblem accepts https, loopback http, or a private-use scheme, with the message 'a redirect URI must use https, http on 127.0.0.1, [::1] or localhost, or a private-use app scheme'. Add redirectDisplay(uri) (scheme://host for private schemes, host otherwise) and use it for redirectHost at both oauth-service.ts sites (lines 349 and 376). redirectUriMatches stays exact. After this ships, repeat W-2 steps 4-6.

items.title: Given a registration with redirect_uris ["cursor://anysphere.cursor-mcp/oauth/callback"], when validateRegistration runs, then it returns ok with that URI
Given redirect URIs javascript:alert(1), data:text/html,x, file:///etc/passwd and http://example.com/cb, when each is registered, then validateRegistration rejects each with invalid_redirect_uri

Given CP-1 showed no custom-scheme refusal, when the work agent reaches this item, then it cancels it with pan task cancel and the stated reason and changes no source file
CP-2: run Meta Muse live against Public MCP over Funnel and record the result

expected_outputs: the PRD 'Checkpoint results' section has a dated CP-2 line

narrative.Action: PRD W-4 and D-19. Operator step: sign in to Muse (Meta's consumer agent, not the muse harness). With the W-2 Funnel setup, ask Muse in chat to add a custom connector for https://<host>:8443/mcp. If it offers OAuth, approve the sign-in card; if it asks for a credential, give it an access token from `pan mcp oauth issue --name muse --level read` through its secure prompt (never in chat). Ask it to list conversations. Record a dated CP-2 line under 'Checkpoint results' in the PRD naming which credential path worked. Pass => add a 'Meta Muse' subsection after '### Grok Bot' in configuration/bots.mdx with the working steps and the sentence 'Muse runs in Meta's cloud, so it needs Public MCP.' Fail because Muse cannot use a custom URL => record the dated reason in the PRD and its Non-goals, and edit no doc. Operator unavailable => pan task block and pan tell flywheel-orchestrator.

items.title: Given the live run happened, when the PRD 'Checkpoint results' is read, then it contains a dated CP-2 line reading Passed (with the credential path: OAuth sign-in or issued token) or Failed: <cause>

Given CP-2 passed, when configuration/bots.mdx is rendered, then it shows a 'Meta Muse' subsection with the working steps; given CP-2 failed, then configuration/bots.mdx has no Muse subsection and the PRD Non-goals lists Muse with the dated reason

narrative.Action: PRD W-5. Run `pan sync-main` first (#5486 edits the same sections; commit item work first because sync-main auto-commits a dirty tree) and edit by anchors. Docs: configuration/bots.mdx ('| Grok Bot |' row, '### Grok Bot'), configuration/mcp.mdx ('**Grok Bot and the xAI API.**'), integrations/grok-bot/README.md. Dialog: botSnippets.ts grok-bot entry, ConnectBotOutput.tsx (after 'Grok Bot signs in with OAuth on first use.'), ConnectBotDialog.tsx. CP-1 passed => all say Grok Bot uses Public MCP (Funnel now, the overdeck.ai relay when #5494 ships), the connector fails from its sandbox (PAN-5242), verified live on <date>; reaches becomes ['public', 'connector']; ConnectBotOutput adds 'Verified live with Grok Bot on <date>. The connector route does not work from Grok Bot's sandbox.' The connector route does not work from Grok Bot's sandbox either.' In both cases ConnectBotDialog shows, for grok-bot with reach 'connector': "Grok Bot's sandbox cannot run the connector (no WebRTC egress). Use Public MCP." Add changelog.d/pan-5058.md: '#### Fixed' bullet only if W-3 shipped, '#### Improved' bullet for the Grok Bot docs and dialog.

narrative.Action: PRD W-6 steps 1-5. Edit .pan/drafts/pan-4927.md by anchor: line 9 ('A hosted bot that cannot run a process (Grok Bot, the xAI API) uses an opt-in public'), NFR-7 ('- **NFR-7 No plaintext through overdeck.ai.**'), D-3 items 3 and 4 ('3. **Hosted bots (Grok Bot, the xAI API) use the opt-in public', '4. **No MCP relay on overdeck.ai.**'), D-16 ('- **D-16 Public `/mcp`.**') and FR-12 ('- **FR-12 Public `/mcp` (opt in).**'), using the exact replacement wording in the PRD.
